newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Dashed reform hopes weigh on India GDRs.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Dashed reform hopes weigh on India GDRs.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) took a beating again on Monday in the wake of continued disappointment about lack of prgress on stock market reforms.

Traders said the market had been hoping that Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram would reveal moves on double tax and dividend policies before leaving for the Davos World Economic Forum in Switzerland last Friday.

On Thursday, he announced the decision to allow foreign portfolio investment in debt and government gilts, among other measures, some of which had been announced through January. But many investors had expected something more.
Bombay's top 30-share index falls 56.83 points, or 1.68 percent to 3,325.64, off intra-day high of 3,382.47
"There has been a heavy shake-out in the local market and continued weakness," said one trader. "Basically it looks like they (the government) have run out of ideas."

"The government has been talking up the market for a while and most of the run up in January was speculative. Now people are unwinding those positions. Volume is reasonable but there is little being delivered, it's all speculative."
At midday, the Cazenove Indian GDR Index was down 0.19 points, or 0.26 percent at 71.96. The premium for GDRs over stocks on the local market was 11.69 percent after 9.82 percent on Friday.

Blue chip stocks were hit hardest, especially State Bank of India (SBI) which took a hammering, down four percent on the day at around 17.75. Others which moved lower were Indian Hotels, Tata Engineering and Reliance Industries. The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 1.20 points or 1.84 percent at 64.22 points, with the premium over the local market at 12.11 percent.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 1.16 percent at 67.68 with a premium of 49.84 percent over the local market, while the Capel Taiwan GDR Index closed 0.05 percent lower at 102.91 with a premium of 6.25 percent.
